A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BC-IB research, despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CortexBench and LIBERO experiments, sensitivity and few-shot analyses, and real-world robot results in Appendix C.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds CogAct robot experiments, a diffusion-policy comparison, and attention-map analyses.

M1.justification: The MINE estimator, fusion framework, and core IB objective are retained. Appendix C.3.1 adds an architectural extension that replaces BC-Transformer's 1.14M-parameter MLP policy head with a 90M-parameter diffusion head, without redesigning the central IB approach.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's two single-task cup manipulations, v3 adds language-conditioned real-world placement involving corn, a wood block, different bowls, distractors, randomized positions, and unseen object–bowl combinations. This substantially extends the evaluated task and generalization conditions. The CortexBench and LIBERO task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated CogAct versus CogAct+IB comparisons in the real-world multi-task setting and DP versus DP+IB on LIBERO-Long. These extend comparison to substantially different policy families. The original simulation comparators and real-world VC-1 comparison remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include 800 real-world demonstrations, 10 evaluation trajectories per task, and CogAct training for 8,000 steps with batch size 128. The added diffusion experiment uses a 90M-parameter head, 50 epochs, batch size 64, and beta=1e-5. Existing simulation splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds attention-map case studies on four tasks, an investigation of policy-head capacity on LIBERO-Long, and real-world tests involving unseen combinations. These examine mechanisms, capacity limitations, and generalization beyond v1's analyses. The existing fusion, beta-sensitivity, mutual-information, and few-shot analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: The retained simulation comparisons use the same three-seed reporting and mean-plus-standard-deviation summaries. The new CogAct and diffusion-policy comparisons provide point estimates without introducing additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original simulation tables and single-task robot outcomes are unchanged. New results include DP at 78.0 versus DP+IB at 84.0 on LIBERO-Long (Table 10), and CogAct averages of 60% versus 70% with IB (Figure 4c). The latter includes ties and a 100%-to-80% decline on the unseen wood-block/blue-bowl task. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical model settings.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, equations, Theorems 4.1–4.3, and Appendix A proof are retained. Section 4.3 rewrites the explanation connecting the intermediate-feature bottleneck to input-level information, but introduces no new bound, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: studying latent redundancy, applying IB to behavior cloning, improving generalization, and providing theoretical justification. Replacing 'significant' with 'consistent' improvements and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v1 attributes weak long-horizon gains partly to compression disrupting sequential dependencies; v3 instead emphasizes limited baseline capacity. v3 also adds explanations involving low TriFinger redundancy and selective attention, revises the LIBERO-Object hypothesis toward data quality, and updates scalability and policy-head limitations to acknowledge the new experiments.

D1.justification: v3 adds real-world training details, diffusion-policy settings, and disclosure of unfiltered 128×128 LIBERO images. Appendix B.3 updates GPU/CUDA information and documents eight-A100 training for the multi-task robot setting. Existing hyperparameter tables and the project link remain; these disclosures do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges prior IB use for copycat problems in behavioral cloning, adds references supporting its contrast with earlier bottleneck approaches, and includes CogAct and additional policy-background citations. The Octo reference is removed. These are focused extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Latent Representations' to 'Latent Redundancy.' Sections 4.1 and 4.3 receive expanded explanations, real-world evaluation gains a main-text subsection, and appendix analyses are reorganized. An impact statement and localized language edits are added, while the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 expands the earlier robot display into Figure 4, adds attention-map Figure 11 and a diffusion-results table, and relocates existing few-shot plots: v1 Figure 11 becomes v3 Figure 7, while v1 Figure 6 becomes v3 Figure 12. Most existing plots, table formats, and the overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left diffusion heads and large vision-language-action policies untested, with real-world evidence limited to two cup tasks. v3 substantially strengthens practical validation through the LIBERO-Long diffusion comparison and CogAct tests involving language conditioning and unseen combinations. These address important gaps in applicability, although missing uncertainty reporting limits the new evidence, and changing both head type and size leaves the capacity explanation tentative.
